text:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change rolled last night we're seeing a regression on 4xTP configs (TP+PP mixed) with FP8 enabled. Throughput down ~18%, frequent all-reduce stalls in the timeline. attaching quick nsys snapshot excerpt below.

raja: ugh. which selector change? commit hash? can you paste the nsys slices or top timers?

maya: commit 0a1b2c4 -> selector picks 'fast_matmul_v2' for sharded linear when seq_len < 512 now. nsys slice shows lots of gap before allreduce starts:

````
# timeline excerpt (simplified)
GPU0: matmul(10ms) -> gap(8ms) -> allreduce(12ms)
GPU1: matmul(10ms) -> gap(9ms) -> allreduce(11ms)
... repeated on every step
NVLINK bursts happening at the end of matmul instead of overlapped with matmul compute
````

liam: that gap looks like we lost our comm/compute overlap. selector_v2 probably changed kernel tiling so matmul finishes later and reduces overlap window.

devon: also saw weird KV behavior in the same runs: cache hits spike then KV resharding shows a barrier. could be batching heuristic interacting with TP sharding. maya can you paste batching config?

maya: batching: {"max_batch_tokens": 4096, "pad_to_multiple": 128, "batch_timeout_ms": 8} — we have aggressive small-timeout canary enabled. KV pattern: frequent short prefixes from chat workloads, lots of incremental KV writes.

raja: quick hypothesis: new kernel increases per-sample latency slightly, batcher times out and flushes partial batches more often, causing more, smaller allreduce ops (higher overhead). plus a KV reshard sync when a new slice is created.

liam: Agreed. Another angle: FP8 scaling. We noticed a few steps where scale resets cause larger exponent ranges -> quantized chunk sizes change alignment. That can break NCCL buffer coalescing and force extra allreduce calls. Haven't proven it yet.

maya: i ran a short experiment: rollback selector -> throughput back to baseline. flip FP8->INT8 emulation (software quant path) -> overlap returns but quality differs. So it looks like selector *and* quant path interact.

devon: for immediate mitigation: revert selector change in canary pool, and disable aggressive batching timeout for 4xTP customers. long term: make kernel selector aware of comm overlap (prefer kernels with earlier outputs for overlap).

raja: agree. can we add a perf test in CI that runs 4xTP + FP8 under our small-prefix chat workload? current perf suite didn't catch it because it used longer sequences.

liam: i'll add a micro benchmark (seq_len distribution skewed to short prefixes) and include NCCL timeline assertions. also add a test that toggles quant scale hook to ensure buffer layout deterministic when scale resets.

maya: thanks. pinned logs: /srv/snapshots/1769802468_nsys.zip and short perf csv: /perf/runs/1769802468.csv. I'll open a follow-up PR to revert selector in canary now.

infra-bot: canary-revert: started rollback of deployment selector-service -> tag v2.3.1 -> targeting eng-runtime-canary-01..03.

raja: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) revert in canary + monitor (maya), (2) add short-prefix perf test (liam), (3) investigate kv reshard triggers (devon). ping me with small reproducer if you need infra traces. :thumbsup:
